mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces the real discount rate applied to equities, thereby depressing near-term expected returns and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the FEDFUNDS > 4% phase.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the same month
failure_condition: Rank IC > 0.05 over the 60-day horizon or SPX 60-day returns are not outperforming the risk-free rate (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in retail sales (HOUST) accompanied by a surge in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust aggregate demand, which accelerates corporate investment and boosts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 5% month-over-month and INDPRO increases by > 2% simultaneously
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the demand signal (p-value < 0.05 two-tailed).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months suggests supply-side constraints, which typically precede inflationary pressures and lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers sharply in the following month with SPX 20-day returns turning positive (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months during a tightening cycle, the expectation of future wage growth rises, prompting higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% and remains below for two months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite UNRATE in tightening regime (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a labor market imbalance favoring employers, which can fuel wage growth and equity risk premia, producing positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 20% in a month while UNRATE remains unchanged
failure_condition: 60-day returns underperform the risk-free rate (t-test p > 0.05) or unemployment rises while openings decline.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% suggests central banks are comfortable with price stability, reducing policy rate cuts and keeping discount rates steady, which tends to cap equity valuation expansion and yields negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 2% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns exceed +2% during the low-inflation period (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (HOUST) both fall sequentially for two months, it signals weakening demand and supply-side frictions that can depress corporate earnings expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases followed by HOUST decrease in the same month, repeated for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) despite the supply signal.
